title: Select delay compensation for a conveyor oven
equipment: Continuous food-drying conveyor with recirculated heated-air duct
principalTechnique: Robust ordinary PI, measured-load feedforward, Smith prediction, and deterministic measured-feedback fallback
objective: Identify and validate the delayed oven, qualify ordinary PI, feedforward, and Smith candidates from time and frequency evidence, then retain an unapplied architecture that survives declared mismatch and fallback tests.
physicalPurpose: Control downstream product temperature while separating measurable upstream load compensation from prediction of heater action still in transport.

simplifications: One local first-order-plus-dead-time heater-to-product path is used around fixed product, airflow, belt-speed, and moisture conditions.

The qualified upstream disturbance and compensating heater action are combined as independent physical thermal inputs before the common transport-delay model; controller quality can remove feedforward but cannot remove plant load.
The ideal bounded heater includes lag and slew but omits installed heater, fan, recirculation, and power-stage nonlinearities.
Product moisture, drying kinetics, spatial gradients, belt mechanics, fire protection, and functional safety are outside the model.
All results are Simulation evidence and do not authorize a physical oven, belt, fan, or heater.

baseline.limitation: The strongest ordinary PI that passes the robustness envelope still misses the required delayed setpoint rise and cannot act before a measured upstream load reaches the downstream sensor.

change.decision: Use feedforward only for qualified upstream temperature and prediction only while model evidence is valid; otherwise retain the strongest robust measured-feedback PI.

disturbances: Apply a qualified -2 degC upstream inlet-temperature deviation at 54 seconds; the common delayed thermal-input path makes its physical effect begin downstream at 70 seconds.
Repeat with moderate actual gain 0.76 degC/%, time constant 13 seconds, and delay 17 seconds while retaining the nominal internal model.
Repeat with severe actual gain 0.60 degC/%, time constant 18 seconds, and delay 22 seconds to exercise measured-feedback fallback.
Exercise invalid upstream and downstream quality, incomplete or invalid model evidence, unavailable heater, Manual return, ControlledStop, restoration, and rollback.

acceptance.window: time from the 10-second request until first reaching 33.5 degC
mean absolute error from 170 through 180 seconds after settling qualification

abortPredicates: Required temperature, upstream load, model, history, quality, heater, mode, timing, or feedback data are nonfinite, stale, invalid, or outside the declared envelope.
Measured or predicted temperature leaves 15 through 60 degC or requested/applied heater leaves 0 through 100 percent.
Prediction remains active with incomplete history, invalid model evidence, or correction at the 5 degC boundary.
Selected heater authority is unavailable, applied slew exceeds 10 percentage points per second, or restoration fails.
Revision 81 changes without separate explicit application approval.
Simulation evidence is presented as product-quality, fire-protection, heater, belt, fan, or physical commissioning evidence.
safety.restorationMode: Close the simulated heater, restore qualified downstream and upstream signals plus heater availability, fall back to measured feedback, align automatic state to applied heater power, restore 20 degC, then explicitly re-enter Automatic.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process-control engineer with product, thermal-process, heater, airflow, belt, electrical, operations, fire-protection, and functional-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Do not operate a physical oven, heater, fan, damper, or conveyor from this lesson.

Physical experiments require independently reviewed product limits, heater and airflow capacity, belt state, fire protection, topology, excitation, abort, restoration, approval, and rollback immediately before action.
Applying revision 81 requires separate explicit approval and a rollback-ready commissioning window.

video.viewerOutcome: Select and defend an oven delay-control architecture from identification, time, frequency, disturbance, mismatch, and fallback evidence.

learning.context: Three equivalent food-drying conveyor ovens expose the same downstream temperature after a sixteen-second heated-air transport delay.
learning.reason: The strongest robust ordinary PI waits for downstream evidence, while a qualified upstream load and a validated internal model provide two different kinds of earlier information.
theory: FOPDT identification distinguishes process gain, response time, and physical transport delay.
Bode, Nyquist, and delay margin qualify the ordinary measured-feedback controller and its fallback stability.
Feedforward addresses only the measured upstream disturbance that shares the transport path.
Smith prediction estimates current delay-free output but returns authority to measured feedback when model evidence is invalid.
learning.workedPrediction: A 10-percent heater step produces an eventual 8 degC rise after 16 seconds; a -2 degC upstream event requires +2.5 percent feedforward; the delay ratio is 1.333.
practicalPreparation: Declare equipment, delayed paths, units, signal quality, model envelope, history, heater authority, modes, limits, aborts, rollback, and Simulation class.
Predict ordinary, feedforward, and predictor behavior before running equivalent records.
learning.baseline: Reject the next-aggressive candidate and retain the strongest ordinary PI that passes time and frequency robustness requirements.
learning.change: Add qualified upstream feedforward for the measured disturbance, then Smith prediction only for the remaining delay-limited setpoint requirement.
learning.comparison: Classify setpoint, regulatory, mismatch, fallback, invalid, saturated, rate-limited, and not-settled intervals before ranking defined measures.
learning.validation: Validate nominal equivalent copies, ordinary margins, feedforward timing, moderate mismatch, severe fallback, invalid signals, unavailable heater, Manual return, ControlledStop, and unchanged revision.
learning.explanation: Trace measured upstream load through feedforward and heater transport, and trace model-estimated current temperature through prediction, correction, fallback, applied heat, and downstream measurement.
learning.transfer: Lesson 82 asks how the workflow changes when two manipulated variables and two measured outputs interact.
